title: CVE-2026-133985 — TRENDnet TEW-657BRM restore_config.cgi out-of-bounds
summary: Affected: TRENDnet TEW-657BRM A flaw has been found in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. Affected by this issue is some unknown functionality of the file /usr/sbin/restore_config.cgi. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The vendor explains: "I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know." This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

title: CVE-2026-84185 — Jwcrypto: jwcrypto: general json jws kid binding bypass during jwkset verification
summary: Affected: Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI), Red Hat OpenStack Platform 16.2 A flaw was found in the jwcrypto library, which is used for implementing Javascript Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) standards. The issue occurs when the library verifies a General JSON Serialization JWS using a set of keys. Due to a coding error, the library fails to correctly identify the specific key ID (kid) and may instead accept a signature made by any valid key in the set. This can allow an attacker with a valid key to bypass authorization checks in applications that rely on the key ID to identify specific tenants or users.

title: CVE-2026-83495 — Trainer: trainer: trainjob env passthrough enables valuefrom.secretkeyref injection for namespace secret exfiltration
summary: Affected: Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) A flaw was found in the Trainer v2 TrainJob API. A user with permissions to create TrainJobs can exploit this by injecting `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` into environment variable definitions. This allows them to read and exfiltrate sensitive information (secrets) from the namespace, leading to a privilege escalation. This occurs when the TrainJob Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is broader than the Secret read RBAC.

title: CVE-2026-83494 — Training-operator: pytorchjob validateupdate casts oldjob from newobj, bypassing managedby immutability (asvs v5.1.3; u…
summary: Affected: Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) A flaw was found in the training-operator. An incorrect object casting in the PyTorchJob ValidateUpdate webhook allows users to bypass an immutability check. This vulnerability could enable users to detach a queued job from its quota management system or hijack a running job's controller ownership. The primary impact is a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

title: CVE-2026-83493 — Distributed-workloads: github actions pinned by mutable tag/branch, including third-party snyk/actions/setup@master
summary: Affected: Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) A flaw was found in distributed-workloads. A remote attacker could exploit a vulnerability in the pull_request_target workflow by submitting a specially crafted pull request. This workflow processes untrusted code from the pull request author while operating with the base repository's sensitive secrets, such as the SNYK_TOKEN, and its default write token. Consequently, an attacker could exfiltrate these secrets, leading to unauthorized access to the Snyk integration and potential control over the repository.

title: CVE-2026-82327 — Libsolv: libsolv: out-of-bounds write in repo_write() via unvalidated directory id from vertical/paged .solv filelist d…
summary: Affected: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, Red Hat Hardened Images, Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI), Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4, Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 5, Red Hat Satellite 6, Red Hat Update Infrastructure 4 for Cloud Providers A flaw was found in libsolv, a dependency-resolution library used by RPM-based package managers such as dnf and zypper to work with .solv repository cache files. When libsolv rewrites a .solv cache file, it reads directory-id values from the file's compressed filelist data without validating that they fall within the expected range. A corrupted or specially crafted .solv cache file (for example, one left in a torn state after an unclean system shutdown) can cause an out-of-bounds memory write when a tool such as dnf, yum, or zypper next processes it. Successful exploitation is expected to result in a crash of the affected tool (denial of service); it is not expected to allow arbitrary code execution because the out-of-bounds write always stores a fixed, non-attacker-controlled value.

title: CVE-2026-78367 — Rpm: rpmbuild gettarspec() crafted tar member name → macro injection
summary: Affected: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2 Extended Update Support, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support, Red Hat Hardened Images, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6, Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) A vulnerability was found in RPM's rpmbuild tarball processing. When processing a crafted source archive, the getTarSpec() function in tools/rpmbuild.cc passes an attacker-controlled tar archive member name to rpmExpand() as part of a %{basename:...} macro expression. A specially crafted .spec member name can therefore inject RPM macros, including Lua expressions, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running rpmbuild. This can be exploited when a victim or automated build system processes an attacker-controlled source tarball using rpmbuild tarball mode (such as -ts, -ta, or -tb).

title: CVE-2026-74127
summary: Affected: AMD EPYC™ Embedded 3000 Series Processors, AMD EPYC™ 7001 Series Processors Improper verification of a cryptographic signature in the PSP Boot ROM of AMD Zeppelin (Zen1/Zen+) processors could allow an attacker with local access to the SPI flash to bypass secure boot authentication, potentially resulting in arbitrary unsigned code execution at full Platform Security Processor privilege, loss of confidentiality, loss of integrity of the host boot chain, and persistent loss of availability.

title: CVE-2026-40671
summary: Affected: AMD Instinct™ MI300A Series Processors, AMD EPYC™ 9004 Series Processors, AMD EPYC™ 7003 Series Processors, AMD EPYC™ 9005 Series Processors Incomplete cleanup during VMRUN error handling could allow access to a Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP) guest register state, potentially resulting in information disclosure and impacts to confidentiality.

title: CVE-2026-28235
summary: Affected: AMD Ryzen™ 4000 Series Mobile Processors with Radeon™ Graphics, AMD Ryzen™ 7035 Series Processors with Radeon™ Graphics, AMD Athlon™ 3000 Series Mobile Processors with Radeon™ Graphics, AMD Ryzen™ 7040 Series Mobile Processors with Radeon™ Graphics, AMD Ryzen™ 7020 Series Processors with Radeon™ Graphics, AMD Ryzen™ 7045 Series Mobile Processors with Radeon™ Graphics, AMD Ryzen™ 7000 Series Desktop Processors, AMD Ryzen™ 3000 Series Desktop Processors, AMD Ryzen™ Threadripper™ PRO 3000 WX-Series Processors, AMD Ryzen™ 7030 Series Mobile Processors with Radeon™ Graphics and 21 more Improper address validation in the AMD RAID Configuration Driver could allow an attacker with administrative access to read arbitrary kernel memory, potentially resulting in loss of confidentiality.
